title: Seazn capture beat, v1: POST /api/v1/capture/codes/{code}/beats
description: The phone's heartbeat body (capture QR v2 spec 2026-10-01 §6.3.2; `at` amended §17.5, R5 final, agreed with capture 2026-10-01). Strict: anything malformed is 422, which the phone counts as a failed beat. $defs.answer is the 200 answer (§6.3.3) and $defs.refusal every refusal body. A beat never answers 410 (ask 8). Vendored into the capture repo; its sha256, parity with its zod twin and its fixtures are pinned by apps/web/src/server/api-v1/__tests__/capture-contract.test.ts.

claim.description: "new" or "resume" on a claim beat, otherwise null (§6.5, ask 2). A claim rides only until the pairing's first 2xx, so it is never together with cause "rejoin" (a rejoin follows a 2xx live); the server refuses that pair with 422 (D16).

device.description: {model} on a claim beat, Build.MODEL only, otherwise null; read only on a claim (G0-e, §6.3.2).

sid.description: The session this phone holds, or null (§6.3.2).

at.description: When the phone took the beat: ISO-8601 with any offset; a value with no zone is refused. The server normalises it to UTC before storing it; the phone sends Z (§17.5, R5).

state.description: The phone's own state, in kebab-case (§6.3.2, §4).

cause.description: Why the broadcast this phone holds was started (§6.3.2). Non-null only while sid is non-null (a broadcast is held), otherwise null; never "rejoin" on a claim beat. The server refuses either breach with 422 (D16, capture's field-by-field check 2026-10-01).

stopped.description: A session this phone stopped; only while sid is null (§6.3.2, capture RR3, §6.8.2).

answer.description: The 200 answer to a beat (§6.3.3; amended §17.5, R5 final): a union on `state`. The first precedence row that applies wins: taken, replaced, over, waiting, go-live, live. The common fields (label, scheduledStart, autoAllowed, destinationName, overlayUrl, pollSeconds) are required on waiting, go-live, live and over, and optional on replaced and taken; PR-1's server still sends them on every 2xx (ask 1). sid, startedBy and endReason are omitted where they do not apply, never null.

oneOf.description: The slot is empty, paired or starting; while starting, pollSeconds is 5 (§6.3.3 rows 4 and 5).

label.description: "{side A} v {side B}", or "Match {n}" in the competition's locale while a side is not yet known; at most 200 characters, cut with one "…" (§6.4, W25, §17.6).

scheduledStart.description: fixtures.scheduled_at as epoch seconds, or null when the fixture has none (§6.4, §4).

autoAllowed.description: Whether the server may start the broadcast on its own; always false in PR-1 (§6.4, §7.1).

destinationName.description: The pre-picked destination's label, at most 80 characters cut with one "…"; null when there is none or it is archived (§6.4, §6.7.3, §17.6).

overlayUrl.description: The scorebug overlay page, or null when the org lacks streaming.overlay (§6.4.1, W11, W18).

pollSeconds.description: How often the phone polls and beats, 5 to 300 seconds (§6.6, §6.9).

next.description: Court codes only (§5.3): the court's next streamed match not yet started, so the phone can show "Next: …" while waiting or during a live tail. Omitted, never null, when there is none or on a fixture's code.

label.description: The next match as the phone shows it, "{side A} v {side B}" or "Match {n}", 1 to 200 characters (§5.3).

scheduledStart.description: The next match's scheduled start as epoch seconds; null when it has none (§5.3).

realtime.description: Realtime push nudges (spec 2026-11-24 §2.1): the current pairing's push channel, so the phone beats at once instead of waiting out pollSeconds. Sent for the code's current pairing only, on waiting, go-live, live and over; never on replaced or taken (the caller no longer holds the pairing). Omitted, never null, when there is none, a failed mint included (a failed mint never fails the beat). Join `realtime:{topic}` with private: true and listen for the broadcast event `nudge`, payload {v, reason, at}: v epoch milliseconds, at ISO-8601, reason go-live, stop, replaced, over or next-match; an unknown reason is still a ping. A nudge carries no state: the beat answer stays the only truth and pollSeconds the cadence, and the server shortens no timeout because of a nudge. Each token lives 30 minutes. A new token rides on every current-pairing beat, so a new token is not a refresh signal: keep the joined token and swap it (setAuth) only when it has under 10 minutes left, or on a channel error or refusal. A later waiting, go-live, live or over answer WITHOUT realtime (after a failed mint, say) is no reason to leave: keep a joined channel until its expiresAt, and join nothing new without the object (absent means poll only). On replaced or taken, leave the channel: the pairing is no longer the caller's.

url.description: The Supabase project URL: https, with no userinfo, query or fragment. Derive the websocket (wss) URL from it. Public; the phone bakes in no Supabase config.

apikey.description: The Supabase project's public anon key, sent as the socket's apikey; 1 to 512 characters. Public.

topic.description: The bare topic capture:{pairingId}, the pairing id a lowercase 8-4-4-4-12 uuid; the phone joins realtime:{topic}. A court pairing outlives its matches, so its topic stays the same across them.

token.description: The subscriber JWT for this topic only, 1 to 4096 characters. A secret: never in a record, snapshot, log line or URL.

expiresAt.description: When the token expires, as epoch seconds. The phone times its swap from this, never from a guess of its own clock.

autoRefusal.description: waiting only, court codes only (E2, 2026-11-17): why the server's automatic start of the court's match was refused, the word the Match Day court card shows for the court: no_destination (the destination needs the organiser: reconnect, live not enabled, none picked), no_credit, not_entitled, destination_in_use (another match holds the destination), unavailable (a transient failure; the server retries every 60 s), competition_frozen, or match_stopped (court device check, 2026-11-19: the court's only match in play was stopped by hand — the desk's Stop, this court phone's Stop hold, or a handover — so nothing starts it by itself; the desk's Go live or the phone's own Go live hold starts it again). Omitted, never null, when there is no refusal, once a start succeeds or is in flight, on a session shape, and on a fixture's code. The phone reads an unknown word as no refusal.

expiresAt.description: When the token expires, as epoch seconds. The phone times its swap from this, never from a guess of its own clock.

startedBy.description: go-live only: who asked for the broadcast (§6.3.3, §17.5).

delivery.description: Delivery facts (Task 46, 2026-11-24), so the phone can tell "my camera reaches Cloudflare but the programme is down" from "all fine": what the relay and Cloudflare last said about the session's video. On go-live and live only (the two answers that tell the phone to publish; no other answer admits it), to the slot's current phone, for any session with a fact to tell: a composed session's relay and both its inputs, a passthrough session's camera input only (it has no relay and no programme). Each member is omitted, never null, when it is not known; when none is known the object is omitted, never empty and never null. Plain values only: no URL, host, id, key or token. A phone reads an unknown word in any member as not known. Unrelated to the beat REQUEST's own `delivery` (ok, stalled or unknown: what the phone reports of its own picture) and to the `delivery` key a capture-record line may carry (capture-record.v1): the three only share a name.

relayOutput.description: The relay's output to the programme, as the relay's last beat reported it: connecting, connected or backoff (waiting to retry). Omitted when that beat is older than three of the relay's beats, when it was the relay's final beat, or when it reported none.

programmePhase.description: What the programme shows, as the relay's last beat reported it: waiting, live, frozen (the camera's picture stalled), reconnecting or final. Omitted on the same terms as relayOutput.

fps.description: The programme's frames per second, as the relay's last beat reported it, rounded to a whole number. Omitted on the same terms as relayOutput.

kbps.description: The programme's bitrate in kbit/s, as the relay's last beat reported it, rounded to a whole number. Omitted on the same terms as relayOutput.

cameraIngest.description: The phone's camera feed at Cloudflare: connected, disconnected or errored. It follows the latest live-input notification Cloudflare sent for it, EXCEPT that a disconnected is told connected while the relay's own fresh beat, stored after that notification, shows the camera live (a late notification for a dead connection leg must not hide a camera that is on air). Omitted when Cloudflare has sent none.

programmeIngest.description: The programme feed at Cloudflare (a composed session's only), exactly as the latest live-input notification Cloudflare sent for it says: connected, disconnected or errored; never overridden by the relay's beat. Omitted when Cloudflare has sent none.

oneOf.description: The slot is live, with or without video: keep publishing to sid. No startedBy (§6.3.3 row 7, §17.5).

refusal.description: Every refusal: `code` is the machine word the phone keys its copy on; `message` is a developer string, never shown (§4). 401 code_ended (an unknown code, a wrong tok or an ended code), 404 not_a_stream_code (a malformed code), 426 app_outdated (court codes only, court device check 2026-11-19: a claim beat — claim "new" or "resume" — from a build older than the server's court minimum; it is never paired, and every later claim from that build gets the same answer until the app is updated), 422 invalid, 429 rate_limited (with Retry-After) and 503 unavailable (also a court claim while the server has no court minimum configured). 422, 429 and 503 count as a failed beat (§6.3.2, §10.1).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys its copy on (§4).

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it (§4).

sid.description: already_live only: the session that is already live (§6.3.4, ask 4).

startedBy.description: already_live only: who started it (§6.3.4, ask 4).

code.description: The machine word the phone keys its copy on (§4).

message.description: A plain English developer string; the phone never shows it (§4).
